persona.description: Strong refinance candidate who banks elsewhere. Harborline should transfer; a members-only credit union should point them to membership, not a loan officer.
persona.behavior: You saw an online ad and filled out the form. You bank with a large national bank and have no other accounts anywhere. If asked whether you are a member or customer, say no. You are friendly and cooperative and answer questions clearly. If told you'd need to become a member, ask one question about what that involves, then accept the next step graciously.

transcript.text: Hi Robin, this is Dana, an automated assistant with Bayview Community Credit Union. Thanks for reaching out about refinancing. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time to opt out.
Hi Dana, yes now works! Happy to answer a few questions.
Thanks, Robin. First, are you already a Bayview member, for example with a savings or checking account with us?
No, I'm not a member. I saw your ad online, and right now I just bank with one of the big national banks.

Thanks for letting me know, Robin. Bayview's mortgage loans are for members, and membership is open to people who live or work in the greater Bay County area, or who have a family member who's a member. Joining means opening a savings account with a $5 minimum deposit, and our Member Services team confirms eligibility.

Would you like to keep going with a few questions now, so a member loan officer has your details ready if you join?

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm, and adapt to Robin. Examples: "A ballpark is fine," "If not, that's okay," and the reassurance in [14] that answering "doesn't involve a credit check." The membership explanation in [4] is a bit long for text, but it is clear and necessary.
judge.experience_rationale: Robin's non-member status was handled honestly and without rejection in [4]. Their branch-vs-online question was deferred rather than guessed at in [6]. In [22], Robin learned exactly who will call (Member Services), how ("at the number you're texting from"), and when ("Tuesday around 2pm Pacific").

annotations.note: Discloses up front that Dana is "an automated assistant," checks timing, and gives the STOP opt-out.
Explains membership eligibility neutrally without implying a credit or eligibility decision ("our Member Services team confirms eligibility"), then offers an optional path to keep going.
"I don't want to guess" avoids a potentially inaccurate answer about online account opening and commits to passing the question along.
The credit-band question is framed as a self-estimate with "doesn't involve a credit check," which reduces anxiety without implying any outcome.
The close names the team, the number, the day and time with time zone, and what the call will cover, all without promising eligibility or a rate.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant intake that handled a non-member gracefully and never hinted at rates, approval, or savings. The borrower raised no objections and ended with a concrete, correctly routed Member Services callback.
